summary.headline: LTTS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $305.9 Mn and EBIT margin reached 15.2%, with mid-16% margin targeted by Q4 FY27 or earlier.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue was $305.9 Mn, up 0.3% YoY and down 1.7% QoQ, as the company exited low-margin work and divested SWC (Smart World). EBIT margin rose 40 bps QoQ to 15.2%, the second straight quarter of expansion, with gross margin up 150 bps QoQ. Management said the restructuring is complete, with about $19 Mn annualised revenue exited in Q4 and no further restructuring costs expected. It advanced the margin aspiration to mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and set a 5-year Lakshya 31 plan of 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance given.

+8.3% YoY in USD; +14% YoY in INR

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Q4 EBIT margin 16.1%, up 130 bps QoQ; revenue almost flat QoQ. Over 40% of Q4 large deal wins were in Mobility; management expects growth from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Contributed 36% of FY26 revenue; grew 11% YoY in Q4 and sequentially. EBIT margin 28.7%, steady QoQ. Over 50% of Q4 large deal wins; first $50 Mn+ account reported.

segments.name: Tech (incl. Intelliswift)
segments.commentary: Revenue subdued after exits of non-strategic businesses; EBIT margin 12.6%, up 210 bps QoQ on Intelliswift margin gains and restructuring. FY26 Tech including Intelliswift grew 19.7%.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration to reach mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27; management said it may come earlier.
Lakshya 31 five-year plan: 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin; 12.4% past 5-year CAGR includes SWC, per Rajeev Gupta.
Combined DSO expected at 85-90 days going forward.
No annual revenue guidance; management said 'better than industry' for FY27 and that growth would be largely organic with tuck-in acquisitions.
Headcount expected to add about 500 more billable staff across Q1-Q3 FY27 for forward deployment engineering skills and ramp-ups.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose 522 QoQ to 23,830 at year-end after fresher onboarding; attrition steady at 14.7%.
Offshore mix 53.5%, slightly up QoQ; management sees room for improvement in coming quarters.
T&M revenue mix 66.1%, up from Q3.
Management plans to invest heavily in talent, AI tools, and alliances for Engineering Intelligence (EI), physical AI, SDV and connectivity.
Patent filings exceeded 1,700 in FY26 (673 by LTTS, 1,033 co-authored with clients), of which 237 are in AI/GenAI.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV in Q4 was $182 Mn; FY26 large deal wins were $855 Mn, up 40% YoY; average large deal TCV about $200 Mn over six quarters.
North America grew 12% in FY26; all other geographies grew positively.
Realised rupee about ₹93.43/USD in Q4, a 4.3% depreciation vs Q3.
Automotive: North America showing positive momentum with SDV investments; Europe deals being competed against European majors and Indian peers.
Exits of about $19 Mn annualised revenue (Middle East, Europe, Israel, UK, Telecom Infra low-margin work) completed in Q4; no revenue from these in Q4 and none expected to recur.
Middle East exposure in Plant Engineering is very small per management; no impact expected in the current or next quarter.
Less than 50% of revenue currently comes from the six Lakshya bets; management expects more than 70% in five years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SWC divested, and does continuing-ops reporting exclude it for all FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Telco Infra and Cyber were scaled internationally, but Smart Cities could not be taken global because of local-government work. Continuing-ops figures exclude SWC from all periods for like-for-like comparison; mostly India and some international SWC operations were sold. Restructuring is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16%-17% margin a five-year target or achievable sooner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier as an aspiration; 16%-17% is the Lakshya FY31 band to be maintained over five years, not a reduction.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 13%-15% CAGR show up, and when do $100 Mn+ and several-hundred-million accounts emerge?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance. A $50 Mn+ trailing-12-month account was delivered in Q4, the first in a long time. Build-out to $100 Mn accounts is mostly organic and will take time; Alind Saxena now focuses on large deals and growth markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13%-15% CAGR in USD and does the 12.4% historical figure include SWC?
qa_highlights.answer: The 13%-15% is USD-based, and the 12.4% five-year CAGR includes SWC. Reported-currency targets may be added over time.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the six bets and what investment is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 50% of revenue today comes from the six bets; more than 70% expected in five years. Management will hold an Investor Day later in the year with detail. Investment focuses on EI, SDV, connectivity, and physical AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more restructuring, and what is the reason for the $19 Mn exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said the Q4 exceptional charge covers the $19 Mn annualised exit in Europe, Israel and the UK, with no further restructuring costs expected.

qa_highlights.question: Could a 15% margin come as early as H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and did not commit to H2 FY26; margins have improved from the 13.3%-13.6% discussed 2-3 years ago.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting client conversations and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients are asking for productivity pass-through and AI spend is rising. About 60% of staff are trained on AI tools, with the rest due within six months. Management believes LTTS is 6-8 months ahead of competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any M&A planned and would margins take a hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Only tuck-in acquisitions; no large acquisition is planned. Intelliswift's acquisition has performed well, and margins will be kept within the 16%-17% band.

risks_watch: Automotive recovery is unproven: Europe is losing share and Trucks & Off-Highway remains subdued.
Growth depends on converting the $855 Mn FY26 large deal wins into revenue; management expects Mobility growth from Q1 FY27 and Tech growth thereafter.
Margin path depends on continued Intelliswift improvement and the 16%+ target for Q4 FY27; no timeline commitment beyond 'Q4 or prior'.
Offshore mix (53.5%) and DSO (85-90 day guidance) need to improve further.
Rupee depreciation and hiring of 500 more billable staff could affect margins and utilisation.
Investor Day with detail on the six bets and M&A to come later in the year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the Lakshya 31 plan, with multiple timelines advanced. Cautious on near-term growth ('cautiously optimistic'), and evasive on annual guidance and on the exact share of revenue from the six bets, deferred to an Investor Day.

growth.why: Five-year Lakshya 31 plan targets 13%-15% USD revenue CAGR with 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance; backing is partial (FY26 large deal wins of $855 Mn up 40% YoY and about 500 billable hires planned, but no capacity additions).
